edges.description: Restrictive chest disease is part of DA5, but how PIEZO2 gain of function restricts the chest is not established. Clinical authors suggest involvement of skeletal or respiratory muscles, or reduced thorax expansion from hyperactive PIEZO2 signalling; the mouse model did not report respiratory readouts.
Limited eye movement is a defining feature, but the route from PIEZO2 gain of function to extraocular restriction is not established. Muscle fibrosis has been proposed and not demonstrated.
Ptosis accompanies the ophthalmoplegia in most families; its mechanism is not described in the cited sources.
The signal released from overactive sensory endings that alters tendon and joint development has not been identified.

nodes.description: PIEZO2 is the principal mechanotransduction channel of proprioceptive sensory neurons, which innervate muscle spindles and tendon organs. In mice carrying the equivalent of the DA5 allele E2727del, expressing it only in these neurons is sufficient to reproduce the limb contractures, whereas expressing it only in limb mesenchyme (muscle, cartilage and tendon) is not. The effect requires the allele to be active before the third postnatal week, and botulinum toxin, but not motor-endplate blockade with alpha-bungarotoxin, prevents it. The authors interpret this as an efferent action of the afferent nerve endings, likely through increased exocytosis, rather than increased reflex motor drive; stretch-evoked muscle spindle afferent firing was not increased ex vivo. PROVISIONAL because the evidence is from mice and the secreted signal is unidentified.

nodes.description: Mouse carrying the mouse equivalent of the recurrent DA5 variant E2727del, expressed constitutively or restricted by Cre driver to proprioceptive neurons (Pvalb), all sensory neurons (Advillin, inducible) or limb mesenchyme (Prrx1). Constitutive and proprioceptor-restricted mice develop hindlimb contractures and shortened tendons; mesenchyme-restricted mice do not, and induction after the third postnatal week does not cause joint defects. Botulinum toxin injected into the hindlimb at postnatal days 7 to 10, or a maternal diet enriched in eicosapentaenoic acid, which shortens PIEZO2 inactivation, reduced the defects.

nodes.description: Heterozygous dominant PIEZO2 variants alter the kinetics of the mechanically activated channel rather than abolishing it. E2727del and I802F make PIEZO2-dependent currents recover faster from inactivation, and E2727del also slows inactivation, so the channel passes more current for a given mechanical stimulus. Mutant channels are not constitutively open and are not toxic to cells. Most other DA5 variants have not been tested electrophysiologically. The node name is shared with the Gordon syndrome and Marden-Walker syndrome entries because the lesion is the same.
